culture.textEn: {ko:추석} (Chuseok) is the 15th day of the 8th month of the lunar calendar, so its date on the solar calendar moves each year: in 2026 it is 25 September. Korea's lunar calendar came mainly from China.

sources.title: 2026년 달력자료: 국경일과 공휴일, 음력 (2026 calendar data: national holidays and public holidays, lunar months)
sources.publisher: Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute (한국천문연구원) — 천문우주지식정보
sources.quoteOrLocator: Holiday table (명칭, 날짜(요일)): “추석 9월24일~ 9월26일 (목,금,토)”. Lunar table (음력의 월일, 대소, 월건, 일진, 양력의 월일), row of lunar month 8: “8 1 대 정유 무자 2026 9 11”, so lunar 8/1 is 11 September and lunar 8/15 is 25 September. 24절기 table: “백로 9 7 23 41”, “추분 9 23 9 5”. Page note: “이 자료는 공식 발표 자료가 아닙니다. 공식 발표 자료는 월력요항을 확인해주시기 바랍니다.”

sources.title: 추석 (Encyclopedia of Korean Seasonal Customs entry 추석, topic 5060)
sources.publisher: National Folk Museum of Korea (국립민속박물관) — 한국민속대백과사전, 한국세시풍속사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 정의: “음력 팔월 보름을 일컫는 말. 가을의 한가운데 달이며 또한 팔월의 한가운데 날이라는 뜻을 지니고 있는 연중 으뜸 명절이다.” 어원: “중국인들은 추석 무렵을 중추(中秋) 또는 월석(月夕)이라 하는데,”

sources.title: 음력 2 (陰曆) (Standard Korean Language Dictionary entry 음력 2, noun)
sources.publisher: 표준국어대사전 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary), National Institute of Korean Language
sources.quoteOrLocator: Entry 음력 2 (陰曆) 「명사」 『천문』: “1896년에 양력으로 역법이 고쳐지기 전까지 우리나라에서 공식적으로 사용하였다. 현재에도 설, 추석과 같은 명절 등의 날짜를 정할 때 사용한다. 역법 분류상 태음 태양력에 해당하며,”

sources.title: 역법 (曆法)
sources.quoteOrLocator: 내용 요약: “우리나라는 주로 중국의 태음태양력을 도입하여 사용했다.” 본문: “우리 민족이 오래도록 써왔던 태음태양력은 중국력이다.”

verification.notes:
pass 1 (author sourcing, CM-45 S6, 2026-10-31): the KASI 2026 calendar data page, the Encyclopedia of Korean Seasonal Customs entry 추석, the dictionary entry 음력 2 and the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture entry 역법 read on 2026-10-31. 'the 15th day of the 8th month of the lunar calendar' = 음력 팔월 보름 (NFMK); 'its solar date moves each year' = 음력 is used to set the dates of 설 and 추석 (NIKL) while the official calendar is the solar one; 'in 2026 it is 25 September' = KASI lunar month 8 begins 2026-09-11, so 8/15 is 2026-09-25, inside the KASI holiday 9월24일~9월26일; 'Korea's lunar calendar came mainly from China' = 우리나라는 주로 중국의 태음태양력을 도입하여 사용했다 (AKS). Used in: q1 (the calendar page, its Discover and rounds) and the q1 Did you know? tip.
pass 2 (MAR culture and facts, 2026-10-31): all four pages re-read; each quote found. The calendar page's four days are KASI's: 백로 9/7, lunar 8/1 on 9/11, 추분 9/23, 추석 9/25 (lunar 8/15); KASI marks its table as not the official announcement (월력요항), and the dates were checked to agree with each other (lunar 8/1 + 14 days = 9/25, the middle of the 24-26 holiday). Shared heritage (§5.1): the note says the calendar came mainly from China and never calls it Korean in origin; the NIKL wording 우리나라의 전통 역법 is not used. Outcome: pass, no change.
pass 3 (MAR third pass, 2026-10-31): the drawn calendar names no maker or brand; the institutions are named as on the access date (한국천문연구원, 국립민속박물관, 국립국어원). Outcome: pass, no change.

culture.textEn: {ko:강강술래} (Ganggangsullae) is a circle dance done mostly on Chuseok night: under the full moon, women hold hands and sing as they dance in a ring. UNESCO inscribed Ganggangsullae in 2009.

sources.title: 강강술래 (Encyclopedia of Korean Folklore entry 강강술래, topic 3145)
sources.publisher: National Folk Museum of Korea (국립민속박물관) — 한국민속대백과사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 정의: “가무악(歌舞樂)이 일체화된 강강술래는 주로 추석날 밤에 행해지며, 지방에 따라서는 정월대보름 밤에 하기도 한다.” 내용: “동산에 보름달이 떠오르면 마을의 넓은 마당으로 모인 여자들이 느린 가락에 맞춰 늦은강강술래를 추다가” … “여자들이 손에 손을 잡고 둥글게 원을 그려 돌며 추는 춤은 협의의 강강술래요,”

sources.title: Ganggangsullae
sources.quoteOrLocator: “Inscribed in 2009 (4.COM) on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity”; Republic of Korea; “Under a bright full moon, dozens of young, unmarried village women gather in a circle, join hands” … “sing and dance all night under the direction of a lead singer.”

verification.notes:
pass 1 (author sourcing, CM-45 S6, 2026-10-31): the Encyclopedia of Korean Folklore entry 강강술래 (topic 3145, read through the encyclopedia's own topic API) and the UNESCO element page read on 2026-10-31. 'a circle dance done mostly on Chuseok night' = 주로 추석날 밤에 행해지며; 'under the full moon, women hold hands and sing as they dance in a ring' = 보름달이 떠오르면 … 여자들이; 손에 손을 잡고 둥글게 원을 그려 돌며 추는 춤; 가무악이 일체화; UNESCO 'join hands', 'sing and dance'. 'UNESCO inscribed Ganggangsullae in 2009' = Inscribed in 2009 (4.COM), the element's UNESCO name. Used in: q2 (the festival timetable, its Discover sentence and rounds) and the q2 Did you know? tip.
pass 2 (MAR culture and facts, 2026-10-31): both pages re-read; the quotes match. §5.1: the element was inscribed in 2009 and never proclaimed, so 'inscribed' alone; the UNESCO name is Ganggangsullae. 'mostly' keeps the encyclopedia's 주로 (it is also done on the first full moon in some places); the note leaves out the origin stories, which the encyclopedia calls unfounded, and the unmarried and young wording, so it suits any age. Finding fixed: the draft's 'women hold hands, sing and dance' read as three acts; it now says they sing as they dance, the encyclopedia's 가무악이 일체화 (es cantan mientras bailan; ko 노래하며 둥글게 돌아요). Outcome: fixed.
pass 3 (MAR third pass, 2026-10-31): the drawn poster and timetable name no organiser, park or brand; the 7:00 time is a practice time for an evening dance, not a claim about a real event. Outcome: pass, no change.

culture.textEn: Months are a number with {ko:월}: September is {ko:구월}. Two months are said another way: June is {ko:유월}, not {ko:육월}, and October is {ko:시월}, not {ko:십월}.

sources.title: 한글 맞춤법 제52항 (Hangul Orthography, article 52)
sources.publisher: 국립국어원 (National Institute of Korean Language) — 한국어 어문 규범
sources.quoteOrLocator: 제52항: “한자어에서 본음으로도 나고 속음으로도 나는 것은 각각 그 소리에 따라 적는다.” 예시 (본음으로 나는 것 / 속음으로 나는 것): “오륙십(五六十) / 오뉴월, 유월(六月)”; “십일(十日) / 시방정토(十方淨土), 시왕(十王), 시월(十月)”.

sources.title: 유월 1 (六▽月) and 시월 1 (十▽月) (Standard Korean Language Dictionary entries, noun)
sources.publisher: 표준국어대사전 (Standard Korean Language Dictionary), National Institute of Korean Language
sources.quoteOrLocator: Entry 유월 1 (六▽月) 「명사」: “한 해 열두 달 가운데 여섯째 달.” Entry 시월 1 (十▽月) 「명사」: “한 해 열두 달 가운데 열째 달.” (searchKeyword=시월)

verification.notes:
pass 1 (author sourcing, CM-45 S6, 2026-10-31): Hangul Orthography article 52 and the dictionary entries 유월 1 and 시월 1 read on 2026-10-31. 'Months are a number with 월' = the entries define 유월 and 시월 as the sixth and tenth of the twelve months (六月, 十月); 'June is 유월, not 육월, and October is 시월, not 십월' = article 52 lists 유월(六月) and 시월(十月) as the 속음 written as said, beside 오륙십 and 십일 in the 본음. 'September is 구월' follows the same pattern with no change. Used in: q3 (the ticket's date 구월 이십사일, the window's 구월 이십사일이요) and the q3 Did you know? tip; q1 and q2 read 구월 too.
pass 2 (MAR language, 2026-10-31): both pages re-read; the quotes match. The note teaches the reading only and makes no claim about history; 육월 and 십월 appear as the forms not used, inside {ko:} tokens, and no round asks them. Outcome: pass, no change.
pass 3 (MAR third pass, 2026-10-31): the institution is named as on the access date (국립국어원). Outcome: pass, no change.

notes: Volume 2 MAR (row CM-45 S6, F-CURR-002 9.2, 2026-10-31; passes: author, language, culture and facts, learning design, reviser, third pass). No native-speaker or expert review is claimed; language: native-reviewed is the schema's name for the signed-off language gate.

Language pass: spelling, spacing, particles and 해요체 line by line (추석은 구월 이십오일이에요; 구월 이십삼일은 ___이에요 with consonant-final tiles; ___는 일곱 시에 해요 with vowel-final tiles; 구월 이십사일이요); every romanization is the F-CNT-002 converter's (이십오일 isiboil, 십이번 sibibeon, 음력 팔월 초하루 eumnyeok parwol choharu).

Language pass (cont.): Applied: dates, the seat and the lunar dates are written in Hangul (구월 이십오일, 십이번, 음력 팔월 보름), as Volume 1 writes its hours, so the converter checks each; the clerk asks 몇 시 기차로 드릴까요?; the 강강술래 gloss no longer opens with its romanization; the calendar's alt text says lunar month 8 begins on the 11th, not 8/1 read aloud.

Culture and facts pass: n1 (Chuseok is lunar 8/15, 25 September in 2026; the calendar came to Korea mainly from China) on KASI's 2026 calendar data, the NFMK seasonal-customs entry 추석, the NIKL entry 음력 and the AKS entry 역법; n2 (Ganggangsullae, inscribed 2009) on the NFMK entry and UNESCO; n3 (유월 and 시월) on Hangul Orthography article 52 and the NIKL entries.

Culture and facts pass (cont.): every calendar day is KASI's (백로 9/7, lunar month 8 from 9/11, 추분 9/23, 추석 9/25, holiday 9/24-26), and the ticket's 24 September is the day before Chuseok; the poster, timetable and ticket are drawn and generic (no organiser, park, operator, line or train number); the lunar calendar is never called Korean in origin; suits any age.

Learning design pass: 3 quests; Discover words per quest within the Stage 6 cap of 6 (U-3) and at most 8 new items (lesson-new-load); Practice and Check items from earlier quests at least 30 in 100 in each quest, with the Volume 1 words 추석, 송편, 윷놀이, 출발, 도착, 서울, 대구 and the hours in new contexts; Checks Type Hangul (Dictation), Realia Read (the timetable) and Cloze Pick (ticket values), one of each.

Learning design pass (cont.): triples RR/CP/TH, RR/CP/RR, RR/TR/CP differ from Volume 1's (RR/TH/RR, RR/TH/CP, RR/TH/TH) and adjacent quests differ. Applied: every Practice has four rounds (U-1: the poster's games line, the ticket's departure and its seat line); q3's Check asked the date its Practice had asked and now reads the time and the seat. Each Check reads its own quest's card or words.

Learning design pass (cont.): device voice: the Dictation targets 추석 and 송편 have no sound change and one spelling each, and play their Type Hangul see fallback while game.type-hangul-hear is at pct 0; dates and seats are Sino-Korean (구월, 이십사일, 십이번) and hours native (일곱 시), written as said; 보름 and 초하루 name the lunar 15th and 1st as the NFMK entry does; no number is dictated.
Reviser: applied the fixes above. Third pass: no change. The checker passes ran in one authoring session as separate passes against the checklists of 9.2 and 9.3.
